title: doubleclick tracking cookie is activated when yoast is enabled?
body:
* [*] I've read and understood the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/Yoast/wordpress-seo/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [ *] I've searched for any related issues and avoided creating a duplicate issue.

### Please give us a description of what happened.
The latest version of Yoast is adding a doubleclick.net tracking cookie - the same issue as another user highlighted here: https://wordpress.org/support/topic/doubleclick-cookie-2/

If Yoast 12.9.1 is enabled in my client's wordpress site, I see this in my browser console (firefox):

Request to access cookie or storage on “https://stats.g.doubleclick.net/r/collect?v=1&aip=1&t=dc&_r=…gid=1214148442.1580759106&gjid=2033668700&_v=j80&z=109459827

If I disable the site's theme (Ronneby), then the issue goes away. I am not sure if this is a bug with Yoast or that the theme coders are adding the cookie.

### Please describe what you expected to happen and why.
There should not be any such tracking cookies added to the site when using Yoast. This is a breach of privacy policy and ethics.

### How can we reproduce this behavior?
1. Install and run yoast? I don't know more than that.
2. Load a page in Firefox that is set to block tracking cookies. Then view the console output.

### Technical info
* WordPress version: 5.3.2
* Yoast SEO version: 12.9.1

comments.body:
Hi @propertunist and thank you for your report. I am not sure where the request in your site is originating from, but it isn't from our plugin. We don't use those tracking services.

As such, I am going to close this thread. Feel free to leave any comments below. I hope you're able to track down the source of your issue!
